correctness.rationale: The Jacobi reduction M_s=2/||J_s|| uses the original weighted coefficient form and all approximant zeros (the cited 2016 reduction is prior); weights give edges ((j+3)/(j+2))^(s/2). After scaling first edge to 1, b=(8/9)^(s/2) and c=(5/6)^(s/2). The first two site Schur complement yields λ-1/λ=b²m(λ), λ>1; the tail norm <=2c<1/2 for sufficiently large s and its bipartite resolvent has m=λ^(-1)+c²λ^(-3)+O(c⁴). Thus λ²=1+b²+b²c²+O(b^6), since (160/243)^s and (50/81)^s are <=(512/729)^s, giving the three requested coefficients and uniform error. Principal 2×2 and 3×3 Jacobi compressions yield exact first-degree generator-degree-one/two formulae, not a claim about higher-degree approximants. Resolvent control gives O(b²) spectral mass outside coordinates 0 and 1. Independently diagonalized 1,301×1,301 Jacobi truncations at s=16,20,32,48,64; their absolute remainders divided by specified b^6 were bounded and their quadratic gaps positive. These finite sections corroborate but cannot replace the infinite tail estimate.
